label: server group
type: an administrator-defined grouping of cluster nodes (Enterprise Edition only) that makes replica placement rack- or availability-zone-aware, so that a whole group failing does not take both an active and its replica. The first node of a new cluster is placed automatically in a group named `Group 1`.
aliases_note: `manage:server-group` is filed away from because a `manage:` prefix names a DIRECTORY in the docs tree, not a subject - an id must name its subject, not its location. `capella:server-group` is folded on the strength of its own page's wording, which names no Capella-specific construct: "The distribution pattern is based on a projection of optimal index availability, given the number and disposition of Index Service nodes across defined server groups." 3 + 1 files, zero overlap. The Capella leg is the weaker of the two and is recorded as such.
evidence: Server _groups_ can be administrator-defined to contain a number of the nodes within a Couchbase Cluster, and thereby protect the cluster against large-scale infrastructure failure.
Server groups and the Server Group Awareness feature are only available in Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition.
when you initialize a new Couchbase Server cluster, the first node is automatically placed in a server group named Group 1.
Starting with Couchbase Server release 7.0.2, the Search service supports Server Groups/Rack zone aware replica placement.
